title: CVE-2026-11586: WS Auto-PONG memory exhaustion
explain: The real code shows the flaw the report describes.
summary: A remote WebSocket peer can cause curl to exhaust memory by sending legal PING frames while refusing to read the client's automatic PONGs, leading to unbounded growth of the auto-PONG send queue.

claims.text: curl automatically replies to each received WebSocket PING with a PONG unless CURLWS_NOAUTOPONG is set
claims.reasoning: The flag CURLWS_NOAUTOPONG exists and is documented as disabling automatic PONG responses. The default behavior (flag not set) is to auto-reply to PING with PONG.

citations.note: CURLWS_NOAUTOPONG flag defined; the auto-PONG behavior is the default when this flag is not set

claims.text: In lib/ws.c, ws_enc_add_cntrl() queues the generated PONG into ws->sendbuf and ignores the result of ws_flush()
claims.reasoning: ws_enc_add_cntrl stores the PONG in ws->pending, then if not in the middle of another frame, calls ws_enc_add_pending (which queues it to sendbuf) and ws_flush, but discards ws_flush's result.

citations.note: Calls ws_enc_add_pending to queue the PONG frame
Calls ws_flush but explicitly ignores its return value with (void) cast

claims.text: A malicious WebSocket peer can complete a valid upgrade, stop reading client data, and keep sending legal PING frames
claims.reasoning: The code accepts PING frames up to the protocol maximum (125 bytes payload). A peer can complete the handshake (valid upgrade) then send a stream of legal PING frames while not reading the connection, causing curl to queue PONG responses.

citations.note: PING frame payload length checked against WS_MAX_CNTRL_LEN (125 bytes), so legal PING frames are accepted
Frame type stored in ws->pending.type; PING frames trigger auto-PONG via this path

claims.text: curl continues appending internal PONGs without an effective hard limit, causing memory exhaustion
claims.reasoning: The send buffer is initialized with BUFQ_OPT_SOFT_LIMIT (only a soft limit), and ws_flush's result is ignored, so there is no effective hard limit on how many PONGs can be queued when the peer stops reading.

citations.note: BUFQ_OPT_SOFT_LIMIT defined as a soft limit flag (allows growth beyond the nominal limit)
ws_flush return value ignored, so backpressure from a full send buffer is not propagated to stop accepting new PINGs

claims.text: The provided PoC reproduces the issue by sending 65536 PING frames and hitting out-of-memory within seconds
claims.reasoning: The PoC sends 65536 empty PING frames (2 bytes each). Each triggers a PONG queued to the soft-limited sendbuf. With the peer not reading, memory grows rapidly until OOM, as the report demonstrates.

citations.note: PING payload length limit WS_MAX_CNTRL_LEN allows the 2-byte empty PING frames (�) used in the PoC
Each PING triggers a PONG queued to sendbuf; with ws_flush ignored, the queue grows unbounded

claims.text: The vulnerability can cause curl to exit with (27) Out of memory under memory limits
claims.reasoning: Under a memory limit (180 MiB RLIMIT_AS), the unbounded queueing causes allocation failure, which curl reports as CURLE_OUT_OF_MEMORY (error 27). The control with CURLWS_NOAUTOPONG does not exhibit the growth.

citations.note: Ignored ws_flush means no backpressure; sendbuf grows until allocation fails
CURLWS_NOAUTOPONG avoids this path entirely, confirming the auto-PONG queueing is the cause

key_reasons: The code shows ws_enc_add_cntrl queues a PONG for each PING and ignores ws_flush's return value (lib/ws.c:648), so backpressure from a full send buffer is lost.
The send buffer is initialized with BUFQ_OPT_SOFT_LIMIT (lib/bufq.h:111), which permits unbounded growth beyond the nominal limit.
A remote peer needs only to complete a valid WebSocket handshake, then send legal PING frames while not reading; curl will queue PONGs until memory exhaustion.
The PoC demonstrates ~1 GiB RSS in ~2 seconds and OOM (error 27) under a 180 MiB address-space limit, even with --max-time 8.
CURLWS_NOAUTOPONG avoids the vulnerable path entirely, confirming the auto-PONG queueing is the root cause.
This is not a 'never-ending transfer' (which curl policy excludes) but a rapid, attacker-driven memory exhaustion DoS reachable from a remote peer without API misuse or malformed frames.
reply: Thank you for the detailed report and reproducible PoC. The code confirms that ws_enc_add_cntrl() queues an automatic PONG for each received PING and discards ws_flush()'s return value (lib/ws.c:648), while the send buffer uses only a soft limit (lib/bufq.h:111). This allows a remote peer to drive unbounded memory growth by sending legal PING frames after a valid handshake while not reading the connection. The PoC demonstrates OOM (error 27) within seconds even with --max-time 8. This is a valid remote DoS via memory exhaustion. We will prioritize a fix that adds a hard limit or backpressure to the auto-PONG queue.
